subject: Order form: billing window, VAT treatment, and min-commit phasing
messages:
From: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@stellix.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-20T14:12:00Z
Subject: Draft order form questions on billing window and VAT

Diego —

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form (attached). A couple of quick items the finance team asked us to confirm before we run this through procurement: 

1) Billing window: the draft implies a monthly invoice for committed spend but also references an "activation fee" billed up front. Can you confirm whether the activation fee is invoiced immediately at signature and whether monthly invoices will be in arrears or in advance? Our treasury needs clarity to map cashflow.

2) VAT / EU tax: we are an EU entity (Stellix Ireland). The Order Form currently lists tax responsibility as "customer" but doesn't include a VAT certificate. Please confirm how Redwood will treat VAT (reverse charge vs. Redwood charging VAT).

3) Minimum commit phasing: our procurement wants the option to phase the annual minimum commit over three quarterly tranches in the first year. Is that acceptable, and will that change invoicing cadence or the activation proration?

We want to avoid back-and-forth in legal if we can. Can you point to the standard billing path and what evidence you need? I can loop in Samir from procurement if helpful.

Best,
Emma Rogers
Head of Finance, Stellix Health
emma.rogers@stellix.com

Attachment: OrderForm_STX_v1.docx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2025-05-20T15:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Draft order form questions on billing window and VAT

Kimberly / Karthik —

Forwarding Stellix's finance questions (below). Quick summary of asks they want resolved before procurement:

• Confirm activation fee timing and whether monthly invoices are in arrears or advance.
• VAT handling for an Irish entity — they can provide a VAT cert if we require it.
• Whether we can support phasing the annual minimum commit into three quarterly tranches and how that affects invoicing/proration.

My provisional answers (for context):
• Activation fee — we typically invoice activation upon signature (upfront) and monthly committed invoices are in arrears. But I need legal confirmation that activation fee is non-refundable and whether we should show it as "activation/one-time" on invoice.
• VAT — for EU customers we generally accept a reverse-charge treatment when we have a valid VAT registration for the customer. We ask for a VAT certificate on file; billing will show net amount and VAT as 0 if reverse-charge applies. Need tax ops to confirm exact evidence required.
• Min-commit phasing — I think commercial is OK with triage phasing but needs to confirm whether proration affects the activation fee or if charges are pro-rated across invoices.

Can you prepare a short redline or note we can send back to Stellix confirming the billing flows and evidence required? I've attached their draft order form.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
DiegoFernandez@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: OrderForm_STX_v1.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-21T10:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft order form questions on billing window and VAT

Diego —

Thanks for the heads up. I reviewed the draft and prepared notes and a minimal redline to reduce legal churn. See summary below and attached redline (redline_orderform_v2.docx). Key positions: 

1) Activation fee: we will invoice the activation fee at signature as a one-time, non-refundable fee. We'll add explicit language to the Order Form: "Activation fee is invoiced upon Effective Date and is non-refundable except as set forth in the MSA." This avoids ambiguous treatment during cancellation.

2) Monthly billing cadence: monthly invoices will be issued in arrears for usage/committed spend unless parties elect a pre-pay arrangement. We'll add invoice labeling guidance so finance can map arrears invoices to periods.

3) VAT / EU customers: our standard approach is reverse-charge where the customer supplies valid VAT registration and is established as an EU taxable person. Please request Stellix provide a VAT registration certificate and signed tax form (we accept EU VAT cert + business registration). When reverse-charge applies, invoices will show net amounts and a VAT note referencing the applicable reverse-charge directive. If the customer cannot supply evidence, Redwood will charge VAT per UK/EU rules and remit accordingly.

4) Minimum commit phasing: commercial is amenable to splitting Year 1 minimum commit into three scheduled tranches (Q1, Q2, Q3). We'll include a payment schedule appendix showing tranche amounts and invoice triggers. Important: activation fee remains independent (not prorated across tranches). If Stellix requests pro-rated activation, that will need explicit agreement (we are not proposing that by default).

5) Documentation needed: 
  - Stellix VAT certificate (stellix_vat_certificate.pdf)
  - PO or payment instructions for each tranche if they want different remit entities

I attached the redline (track changes) and a brief invoice example for finance. Once Diego gets Stellix's confirmation on VAT cert and tranche remit entities, we can push this to Legal for a quick review (I expect a 24-48h turnaround if we keep the redline limited).

Let me know if you want me to send the redline directly to the customer or if you'd prefer to own the outreach.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.docx, stellix_vat_certificate.pdf

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@stellix.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@stellix.com>, finance@stellix.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-21T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft order form questions on billing window and VAT — proposed path forward

Emma / Samir —

Thanks for the quick questions. Kimberly and I talked through the draft and propose the following path forward to keep procurement moving without involving legal for every small tweak: 

1) Activation fee: invoiced at signature, non-refundable except as per MSA. We'll call it out on the Order Form line-items as "Activation (one-time)."

2) Monthly invoices: issued in arrears. Example: May usage invoiced in early June. We'll include a short billing cadence note in the Order Form appendix so your AP team can map invoice dates to reporting periods.

3) VAT: Please attach a scanned copy of your EU VAT registration (you can reply-all with the PDF). If we receive that, Redwood will apply reverse-charge and issue net invoices with a reverse-charge note. If we do not receive valid VAT evidence, Redwood will charge VAT at invoice. Kimberly attached the specific wording for inclusion in the redline.

4) Minimum commit phasing: Redwood is OK to split the Year 1 minimum commit into three tranches (Q1/Q2/Q3). We'll add a simple payment schedule appendix in the Order Form that lists tranche amounts and invoice triggers. Activation fee is not prorated and will be billed at signature as above. If you need activation to be spread across tranches, let us know and we can route to legal for consideration.

Next steps: Samir, can you confirm the remit entity for each tranche and either attach a VAT cert or state that you will not be supplying one? I can then send the redline (attached) for your review and, pending your confirmation, Kimberly will run a 24–48h legal check. Also attaching the redline we propose for visibility.

Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
DiegoFernandez@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.docx
